As the new school year begins, more Americans now support an outright ban on students using cellphones in classrooms.

The new school year is underway, and the chorus of support for banning iPhones in classrooms continues to grow.

Yes, it's still July, but somehow summer is already over. My kids head back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second consecutive summer where the first day no longer falls in August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion, offering eligible students and educators a gift card worth up to $150 when they purchase select Mac and iPad models before August 27. Consumers in select states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday deals.

While the back-to-school deals are a pleasant surprise, cellphone use during class hours is increasingly unpopular.

Top Comment by GreenPizza

I've seen no data to support allowing students to use cellphones as a way to reduce risk during school shootings. In fact, reducing classroom distractions is what truly allows us to accomplish the purpose of going to school.

A new survey by the Pew Research Center found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using cellphones in classrooms, up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% of people currently oppose implementing bans in classrooms.

Support for stricter, all-day bans prohibiting students from using cellphones throughout the entire school day is rising even faster. For the first time, more Americans support rather than oppose banning cellphone use for the entire school day.

The report also noted that younger adults remain less enthusiastic about classroom and all-day bans, but support has risen across all age groups since 2024. You can read the full report here.

What's your take? Should schools limit iPhone use to classroom hours, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Let us know in the comments.
